summary: Cut strip shows Jupiter shrinking and sliding behind the character with the arm clipping it, and the figure holds a near-frozen T-pose-like stance while the planet moves.

faults.what: Jupiter sits half inside the character's torso and legs; his body and arm pass through the sphere with no wrap or contact.
faults.fix: Offset the planet's path so it stays clear of his body, or put it clearly in front of or behind him in depth.

faults.what: Between 136.06 and 136.09 the planet jumps from the lower-right of the figure to a larger size up behind his shoulders. Its position and scale snap in one frame, and it then shrinks quickly.
faults.fix: Start the planet at the 136.09 position and size, or tween it from the previous frame so the move is continuous.

faults.what: The character holds a stiff, symmetrical T-pose with both arms straight out. It barely changes from 136.09 to 136.29. There is no wind-up or bowling action, so the idea of throwing the planet is not read.
faults.fix: Key a real wind-up and release pose for the arms, with the hand leading toward the planet.

faults.what: The right hand pushes into the planet's surface and sinks into it at 136.26-136.29, with no grip or release.
faults.fix: Place the hand on the sphere surface, or open it so it releases the planet.

faults.what: The legs hang and float with no ground contact or weight shift while the torso stays frozen.
faults.fix: Add hip-led motion and a planted or hopping foot with anticipation and settle.
